$description: The HeyOz component contract. One entry per component: variants, states, the token each state binds per role, and the value that token resolves to in each mode. Generated from the same recipe objects the components compile from, so this cannot describe a component that does not exist.

components.title: Button
components.description: An action committed on this screen, never a route off it. The only recipe that mixes both focus rings, and the only one with a press.

variants.name: primary
variants.intent: The one action the screen exists for. At most one per view.

variants.name: tonal
variants.intent: Brand weight without brand volume. A second brand-coloured action beside a primary, or a primary on a surface that already carries the accent.

variants.name: brand-ghost
variants.intent: A brand-coloured tertiary action. Reads as a link that happens to be a button.

variants.name: inverse
variants.intent: The committing action where brand orange would be wrong: a destructive-adjacent confirm, or a primary inside an already-orange region.

variants.name: secondary
variants.intent: A real alternative to the primary action, not a lesser one.

variants.name: tertiary
variants.intent: One step quieter than secondary, for a row of peers where none should lead. Distinguished from it only by surface step.

variants.name: outline
variants.intent: The boundary is the affordance. For a button on a surface whose colour is not known at author time — a card, an image, a coloured panel.

variants.name: ghost
variants.intent: Tertiary actions that must not compete: toolbar icons, dismiss, cancel.

variants.name: success
variants.intent: Commits something whose outcome is good and worth colouring: approve, publish, accept. Rare — most confirmations are just primary.

variants.name: warning
variants.intent: Proceeds into something recoverable but consequential: overwrite, downgrade, cancel a subscription.

variants.name: destructive
variants.intent: Irreversible. Never the default focus target in a dialog.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring — 120ms, no overshoot. This is the most-executed animation in the system and the one where any delay is read as the product being slow rather than as the animation being long. The press adds a 2% scale on a spatial spring, which is the one place a second spring is justified: the press should feel like the surface gave way, and that is a physical claim about position rather than about colour.

components.title: Icon Button
components.description: A button whose whole label is one glyph. Square at every size, which is the only structural difference from Button — and the reason it needs its own name rather than a prop.

variants.name: primary
variants.intent: The committing icon action. A send arrow, a confirm tick.

variants.name: secondary
variants.intent: The default icon button. A toolbar action that is not the main one.

variants.name: tertiary
variants.intent: One step quieter than secondary, for a dense row of equal actions.

variants.name: outline
variants.intent: The boundary is the affordance. For an icon button on an unknown surface.

variants.name: ghost
variants.intent: A close X, a chevron, an overflow menu. The most common of the seven.

variants.name: brand
variants.intent: An icon action that is the brand doing something: generate, enhance.

variants.name: fixed
variants.intent: Over an image or a video frame, where the surface belongs to the user and neither palette applies. White in both modes.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring, and no press-scale — which is the decision worth stating. Button presses down by 2% because it is large enough that the scale reads as the surface giving way. On a 32px square the same 2% is 0.6px: too small to read as movement, large enough to look like the glyph shifted a subpixel and re-rasterised. The press feedback here is the active fill, which is a full ramp step and unmistakable.

components.title: Button Link
components.description: A text action with no box. Reads as a link and behaves as whichever of the two it is — the tag is chosen by whether the thing it does is navigation or a command.

variants.name: brand
variants.intent: The action a sentence is pointing at. "See full details", "Upgrade now".

variants.name: neutral
variants.intent: A text action that should not draw the eye off the copy around it.

variants.name: subtle
variants.intent: Footer and metadata links. Present, findable, not competing.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring. No press-scale and no entrance: a text action sits inside a sentence or a footer row, and scaling it on press would move the surrounding baseline. The transition is on the colour alone because the underline is always present — there is no thickness or offset animating, which is the usual way a link transition ends up reflowing text on hover.

components.title: Badge
components.description: A status word in a pill. The only component that puts role-coloured text on a role-coloured tint, so the surface underneath it changes what the pairing measures.

variants.name: neutral-subtle
variants.intent: Metadata with no valence: a count, a model name, a tag. The default.

variants.name: neutral-strong
variants.intent: The same thing one surface step up, for a badge on an already-grey card.

variants.name: neutral
variants.intent: Metadata that must be found first: a plan name, a "PRO" marker.

variants.name: neutral-over-image
variants.intent: A label on a thumbnail, a duration on a video frame. The only variant whose backdrop is unknown, which is why its plate is opaque.

variants.name: brand
variants.intent: New, beta, or otherwise ours, where it has to carry. Sparingly.

variants.name: brand-subtle
variants.intent: The same claim inside a list, where a solid orange pill would shout.

variants.name: success
variants.intent: A finished, good outcome that is the point of the row: Ready, Paid.

variants.name: success-subtle
variants.intent: The same outcome in a table of thirty rows that are mostly fine.

variants.name: warning
variants.intent: Needs attention but nothing is broken yet. Near a limit, expiring.

variants.name: warning-subtle
variants.intent: The quiet form: a quota badge that is not yet a problem.

variants.name: critical
variants.intent: Failed or blocked. Something must be done, and this is the one row.

variants.name: critical-subtle
variants.intent: Failed, in a list where several have. Still red, no longer an alarm.

variants.name: info
variants.intent: Neutral system state that should be noticed: Queued, Processing.

variants.name: info-subtle
variants.intent: The same state as ambient information rather than as news.

motion.intent: No pointer states at all — a badge is not interactive — so the transition only matters when a variant changes underneath it, which is exactly when a status updates from Rendering to Ready. effects-default rather than effects-fast because that colour change is information the user should notice, and 120ms is below the threshold where a change registers as having happened.

components.title: Field
components.description: The label, hint and error around a control, and the aria wiring that connects them. Every other form component in this system is built on it rather than repeating it.

variants.name: label
variants.intent: The name of the control. Always present, sometimes only to the a11y tree.

variants.name: hint
variants.intent: What to type, or why the field is being asked for. Persists through errors.

variants.name: error
variants.intent: What went wrong and what to do about it. Never rendered without also setting aria-invalid on the control.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring, and the entrance is a fade with nothing spatial in it. An error message that slides in moves the control above it, and the control above it is the one the user is still typing into — so the travel would be applied to the thing the user is aiming at. Rule 1b keeps opacity on the effects family where the curve cannot overshoot, which matters here because an overshooting opacity clips at 1 and stalls.

components.title: Radio
components.description: One choice from two to about five visible alternatives, all of which stay on screen. Never alone — a single radio cannot be unchecked, so it is a control the user can enter and not leave.

variants.name: unchecked
variants.intent: Not the current choice. The boundary is the whole control.

variants.name: checked
variants.intent: The current choice. Exactly one per group, always.

motion.intent: The ring transitions colour on the fast effects spring; the disc inside scales in on spatial-fast, declared on the disc itself. Same split as Checkbox and the same reason: the container changing colour is a graphic updating, and the mark arriving is a commitment. A radio is also the control most often pressed several times in a row while comparing options, so the colour transition has to be short enough that three presses read as three answers rather than as a fade queue.

components.title: Slider
components.description: A value on a continuous range where the approximate position matters more than the exact number. If the user knows the number they want, they want an input.

variants.name: track
variants.intent: The unfilled remainder of the range. Neutral — it is not an error to be low.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring, and nothing at all on the thumb's position. This is the clearest case in the system for motion being deliberately absent from the thing that moves: the thumb is being dragged, so any easing on its position puts it behind the pointer, and the user reads that as the product lagging rather than as an animation. Rule 1b would also make it wrong twice over — a spatial spring on a dragged element would overshoot past the finger.

components.title: Dropzone
components.description: A file drop target that is also a button. Drag is the affordance people reach for and the click is the one that always works, so it has to be both — a drop-only zone is unusable from a keyboard and on most phones.

variants.name: idle
variants.intent: Waiting. The boundary is the whole control.

variants.name: active
variants.intent: A file is being carried over the zone and releasing it will drop it here.

variants.name: invalid
variants.intent: The last drop was rejected, or the field is required and empty.

motion.intent: Colour only, fastest effects spring. The state change that matters is idle → active, and it happens while the user is holding a file over the zone — a slow transition there means they release before the zone has confirmed it will accept the drop, which is exactly the moment they need the answer. Nothing spatial: a target that grows or lifts as you approach it moves the thing you are aiming at, and unlike a button the aim here is a drop rather than a click, so there is no second chance.

components.title: Tooltip
components.description: A short label for a control whose purpose is not obvious from its icon. It is unavailable on touch and unavailable to anyone who never hovers, so nothing inside one may be information the user needs.

variants.name: default
variants.intent: The only kind. A tooltip with variants is a tooltip carrying meaning it should not.

motion.intent: A fade in on the effects family and nothing spatial at all. The tooltip arrives beside a pointer that has deliberately stopped moving, and any travel would slide it under that stationary cursor — the one case where an entrance actively fights the interaction that triggered it. Rule 1b keeps the opacity on a curve that cannot overshoot, which matters because an overshooting opacity clips at 1 and stalls, and a stalled tooltip reads as the app hanging.

components.title: Popover
components.description: A non-modal panel anchored to the control that opened it, for content the user may interact with. Everything behind it stays live — if it must not, that is a Dialog.

variants.name: default
variants.intent: The only kind. Its content decides what it is; the panel is always the panel.

motion.intent: It scales in from its own centre on the spatial family, which is what `pop` is, and that is correct here for a reason the other entrances are not: a popover has a definite origin — the control that opened it — and pop is the only entrance in the set that reads as emerging from something rather than arriving from a direction. Reduced motion collapses the scale and keeps the fade, so the panel still announces itself without moving.

components.title: Menu
components.description: A list of actions fired from a button. Not a Select — a menu DOES things and holds no value, which is why moving the caret through one must never commit anything.

variants.name: item
variants.intent: An action. Fires and closes the menu.

variants.name: destructive
variants.intent: Deletes something. Never the first item, and never adjacent to a common one.

motion.intent: Colour only on the fastest effects spring, exactly as the listbox row. A pointer crossing a six-item menu fires six of these, so the transition has to be short enough that a fast pass reads as one highlight following the cursor rather than six overlapping fades. Nothing spatial: a row that moves under the pointer changes which row the next click lands on, and in a menu that click deletes something.

components.title: Toast
components.description: Confirmation that something the user already did has finished. It disappears on a timer, so nothing in one may be information they need — if they must read it, it is an Alert, and if they must act on it, it is a Dialog.

variants.name: neutral
variants.intent: Something finished. The default and the commonest by a long way.

variants.name: success
variants.intent: Something finished and the outcome is worth colouring. Rare — most are neutral.

variants.name: warning
variants.intent: Finished, with a caveat the user does not have to act on now.

variants.name: critical
variants.intent: A transient failure that is already being handled. Almost always the wrong choice — see the notes.

variants.name: info
variants.intent: Something changed that the user did not cause.

motion.intent: It rises in on the spatial family, which is the one entrance in this system where travel carries meaning rather than decoration: a toast has no anchor, so movement from off-screen is what distinguishes new information arriving from content that was always there. The colour transition is on the effects family and a tier slower than a button's, because a toast is not being interacted with — nobody is waiting on its hover, so 240ms reads as considered where 120ms would read as twitchy on something that just flew in.

components.title: Input
components.description: Text entry the user submits later. The one component whose smallest size is set by the platform rather than chosen — below 16px, iOS Safari zooms the viewport on focus.

variants.name: default
variants.intent: Every field until the user has done something wrong.

variants.name: invalid
variants.intent: Failed validation. Always paired with a message that says what to do.

motion.intent: Colour only, fast, no overshoot — and no press scale, unlike Button. A text field that moves when you click into it moves the caret you are aiming at, and the caret is a target with roughly one character of tolerance. This is the clearest case in the system for motion that is deliberately absent: every argument for a press-scale on a button is an argument against one here.

components.title: Textarea
components.description: Multi-line entry that grows with its content. Shares Input's bindings by inheritance, so the two can never disagree about what a text box looks like.

variants.name: default
variants.intent: Every field until the user has done something wrong.

variants.name: invalid
variants.intent: Failed validation. Always paired with a message that says what to do.

motion.intent: Colour only, and deliberately nothing on the height. The box changes height as the user types, and that is the one size change in the system that must NOT be animated: a transition on height means the caret arrives at its new line a beat after the character does, so the text and the cursor visibly disagree during fast typing. Input's reasoning about the absent press-scale applies here too, and more strongly — there is more area to move and the same one-character aiming tolerance.

components.title: Select
components.description: A choice from a known, closed set. A real listbox with full keyboard support and typeahead, not a styled native <select> — and not the right component for a set the user can add to.

variants.name: default
variants.intent: Every field until the user has done something wrong.

variants.name: invalid
variants.intent: Failed validation. Always paired with a message that says what to do.

motion.intent: Colour only on the trigger, fastest effects spring, matching Input exactly — they sit next to each other and a different hover speed on two identical-looking boxes reads as one of them lagging. The chevron rotates 180° on open, which is an orientation change rather than travel: it is deliberately not routed through --oz-motion-spatial-scale, because a chevron that stops rotating for a reduced-motion user stops saying whether the panel is open.

components.title: Listbox option
components.description: One row in a floating panel of choices. Its own recipe rather than a helper on Select, so all four of its states are measured by the contrast sweep instead of being chosen by eye.

variants.name: option
variants.intent: One choice. Selected is a wash plus a glyph, never a wash alone.

motion.intent: Colour only, fastest effects spring. The row is the most-hovered surface in any picker — a pointer crossing a ten-item list fires ten of these — so the transition has to be short enough that a fast pass reads as a highlight following the cursor rather than as ten overlapping fades. Nothing spatial: a row that moves under the pointer changes which row the next click lands on.

components.title: Card
components.description: A surface that holds content, and the one component whose variant decides its HTML element: `interactive` renders a `<button>`, the other three a `<div>`.

variants.name: flat
variants.intent: The default. Grouping, no depth claim.

variants.name: raised
variants.intent: Sits above the page: a stat tile, a summary panel.

variants.name: overlay
variants.intent: Detached from the page: popover, menu, tooltip body, dialog.

variants.name: interactive
variants.intent: The whole card is one target. Renders as a button or a link.

motion.intent: Lifts on hover — shadow and a 2px rise together, on the default spatial spring, so the overshoot makes it read as a physical card rather than a box whose shadow changed. Was transition-shadow at duration-base, which animated the shadow while the position snapped; the two are one gesture and now share one spring. The rise multiplies by --oz-motion-spatial-scale, so under reduced motion the shadow still changes and the card stays put.

components.title: Alert
components.description: Something happened, stated in words. The copy carries the meaning and the role colour only sorts it — no two of the four dots separate by more than 1.09:1 in greyscale.

variants.name: info
variants.intent: System state the user did not ask about but should know.

variants.name: success
variants.intent: Confirms the thing they just did actually happened.

variants.name: warning
variants.intent: A consequence they are heading towards and can still avoid.

variants.name: critical
variants.intent: It failed. Say what failed and what to do next.

motion.intent: Enters on the default spatial spring so it reads as arriving rather than blinking into place, and transitions colour on an effects spring. Not `expressive`, deliberately: an alert is often an error, and a bouncy error is a tonal mistake — the motion should be calm precisely when the message is not.

components.title: Dialog
components.description: A question that blocks the screen until it is answered. Four types, and all four look identical — what the type changes is which button commits.

variants.name: basic
variants.intent: A question with a consequence the user can undo. Confirm is neutral.

variants.name: warning
variants.intent: A consequence that is recoverable but costly. Confirm is amber.

variants.name: error
variants.intent: Irreversible. Confirm is red and Cancel takes the initial focus.

variants.name: detailed
variants.intent: The same question where the reason needs a paragraph — a labelled explanation block above the actions.

motion.intent: Enters on the default spatial spring so it reads as arriving rather than blinking into place, and transitions colour on an effects spring. Not `expressive`, deliberately: a dialog is usually asking about something irreversible, and a panel that bounces while it asks whether you want to delete your work is a tonal mistake. The motion should be calm precisely when the message is not.

components.title: Tabs
components.description: A stepped sequence with a progress rail above each label. Built for the onboarding video player, so it lives on an inverse ground rather than on the page.

variants.name: inactive
variants.intent: A step the user has not reached. Reachable, not yet visited.

variants.name: active
variants.intent: The step being watched right now. Exactly one per row.

variants.name: passed
variants.intent: A completed step. Same label weight as inactive; the rail is what differs.

motion.intent: Colour only, on the fastest effects spring. The rail does not animate its width, which is the thing a progress component is usually tempted to do: these rails are chapter extents rather than a completion percentage, so there is no value travelling between two numbers. What changes when the user moves a step is which rail is lit, and that is a colour change.

components.title: Table
components.description: Rows of the same kind of thing, scanned down a column. The row carries every state — the table around it is a border, a radius and a clip.

variants.name: row
variants.intent: A data row. Hoverable and selectable.

variants.name: header
variants.intent: Column labels. Not interactive unless the column sorts.

motion.intent: Row background only, on the fast effects spring. The restraint is the decision: a table is scanned, and anything that moves while the eye is travelling down a column competes with the column. This is also why there is no press scale — a row that shifts under the cursor makes the click target move during the click.

components.title: Skeleton
components.description: A reserved rectangle in the shape of the response, pulsing until it arrives. The only ambient loop in the system, and the only motion the reduced-motion block stops outright.

variants.name: line
variants.intent: A line of text that has not arrived. Width implies the content length.

variants.name: block
variants.intent: A thumbnail, chart or media slot. Matches the real aspect ratio.

variants.name: circle
variants.intent: An avatar. Same token, different geometry.

motion.intent: The only ambient loop in the system, and the only animation with no target to settle toward — which is why it is not a spring. It runs on duration/ambient with a symmetric curve. Now uses the token layer's .oz-ambient class rather than a keyframe defined locally in tailwind.config.js, which matters because .oz-ambient is the marker the reduced-motion block switches off: the local version kept pulsing for anyone who had asked it not to.

components.title: Switch
components.description: A setting written the moment it is thrown. The toggle is the commit — the only control here with no submit step.

variants.name: off
variants.intent: The setting is not applied. Neutral, not an error.

variants.name: on
variants.intent: The setting is applied, right now, without confirmation.

motion.intent: The track changes colour on the fast effects spring; the thumb travels on spatial-fast, declared on the thumb itself below. This is the component the spatial family exists for — a switch thumb that eases to a stop reads as a graphic changing, and one that arrives with a slight overshoot reads as a physical toggle that has been thrown. The travel is ~20px, which is why spatial-fast has the lowest bounce in the family: the same overshoot fraction over 20px is a nudge and over 200px is a flourish.

components.title: Checkbox
components.description: A value collected now and committed by a separate, later act. The only control here with three values, and no click reaches the third.

variants.name: unchecked
variants.intent: Not selected. The default for every row.

variants.name: checked
variants.intent: Selected.

variants.name: indeterminate
variants.intent: Some but not all of the things this controls are selected.

motion.intent: The box transitions colour on the fast effects spring. The tick inside it is the part that should feel physical and it scales in on spatial-fast — see the tick classes in components/ui/Checkbox.tsx, which is the one place a child element carries its own spring. A tick that fades in reads as uncertain; a tick that pops reads as committed, and commitment is the entire semantic content of a checkbox.

components.title: Pricing Card
components.description: One plan, priced, with everything it includes. The only composition in this library rather than a primitive — it is assembled from Button, Badge and ButtonLink rather than binding its own controls.

variants.name: starter
variants.intent: The entry plan. Neutral ground, neutral CTA — it makes no claim.

variants.name: basic
variants.intent: The recommended plan. Brand ground and brand CTA, badged BEST VALUE.

variants.name: professional
variants.intent: The high-volume plan, badged MOST POWERFUL. Binds the neutral surface; its indigo is a decorative wash above it — see TIER_PAINT.

variants.name: enterprise
variants.intent: Done-for-you, neutral CTA — the action is a call, not a purchase. Teal wash over the same neutral surface.

motion.intent: The card itself only transitions colour, on the default effects spring, because the only thing that changes on it is the tint under a mode switch. It deliberately does not lift on hover the way Card.interactive does: the whole card is not a target here, the CTA inside it is, and a card that lifts under the pointer while the button inside it also reacts gives two responses to one gesture and makes the smaller, real target feel less clickable.
